The test uses typical values (0 and 100) and does not explicitly exercise boundary conditions like negative indices, zero-length, Integer.MAX_VALUE, or just-outside-boundary cases.

The test is short and self-contained (<10 lines) with no visible duplicated logic across tests; although there are no helper methods or constants, the brevity and lack of repetition make it acceptable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The method is short (few lines), linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals, indicating low cyclomatic complexity and focused structure.

The test contains more than one assertion (assertNull and assertEquals), which checks multiple properties (returned edge and vertex count), improving fault detection beyond a single superficial assertion.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present; the test appears active and runnable.
The class Javadoc includes traceability information 'Traceability: REQ-GRAFO-001, REQ-GRAFO-002', directly linking tests to requirements.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method uses @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit timing constraint indicating attention to performance-related concerns in the test context.
The method name 'test6' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome, violating descriptive naming conventions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The presence of EvoSuite runner annotations and the generic test name 'test6' and scaffolding indicate the test likely originates from automated generation and retains auto-generated naming; signs of heavy auto-generation are present.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: No Given-When-Then comments, BDD-style naming, or multiple scenario coverage are present; the test appears minimal and focused on a single basic scenario without evidence of prioritized design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises only public API methods of Grafo and does not use reflection or access private/internal state, focusing on observable behavior.
Assertions lack descriptive failure messages and use basic forms (assertNull/assertEquals) without messages; none of the assertions include explanatory messages as recommended.
The test code is concise and has no commented-out code; class-level Javadoc provides intent and traceability but inline comments are minimal (acceptable).
The test contains no sources of non-determinism such as Random, System.currentTimeMillis, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies; it uses deterministic local calls.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only uses local variables and in-memory operations without persisting files or modifying static/shared state; there is no evidence of side effects that would affect other tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: Although the class defines marker interfaces and imports Category, there are no @Category or @Tag annotations applied to the test or class to categorize it for selective execution.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Single Arrange-Act-Assert reduces ambiguity. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if only one Act operation. DECISION: The method calls grafo0.insereAresta(...) and grafo0.grafoTransposto() — two distinct operations/acts. According to rule 1 (if >1 Act operations mark non-compliant) this is non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent. RATIONALE: Allows any-order execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of @Before/@After or only local variables. DECISION: No @Before/@After are present but the test uses only local variables and no shared mutable state is visible. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Test both happy and error paths. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: At least two tests per method (happy + error) or explicit exception tests. DECISION: Only a single happy-path style test exists; no exception or invalid-input test is present. According to rules this is non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test boundary values. RATIONALE: Many bugs occur at edges. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of 0, -1, empty, max values etc. DECISION: The test uses 0 as input which is a boundary-like value; the presence of zero satisfies the evaluation criteria. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be modular and reuse helpers. RATIONALE: Reduce duplication. EVALUATION CRITERIA: helper methods or constants or short unique tests. DECISION: The test is short (<10 lines) and doesn't duplicate visible logic across multiple tests. No helper methods are necessary for this single short test. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and simple. RATIONALE: Easier to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: method length <20 lines and no loops/conditionals. DECISION: test8 is short (~6 lines) with no loops or conditionals. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive. RATIONALE: Single superficial assertions can miss faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: >=2 assertions or checks of multiple properties. DECISION: This test has a single assertion (assertEquals on numVertices) and no additional property checks; per rule 1 (only one assertion -> non-compliant) mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or disabled tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests hide issues. EVALUATION CRITERIA: absence of @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests. DECISION: No @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test annotations are present. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should map to requirements. RATIONALE: Enables coverage traceability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: annotations or Javadoc with requirement IDs. DECISION: Class-level Javadoc includes 'Traceability: REQ-GRAFO-001, REQ-GRAFO-002', which satisfies the criteria. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests separate from functional tests. RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements require separate tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: look for timeout assertions or security checks. DECISION: This is a unit functional test; no performance/security expectations are relevant here and no explicit performance/security tests are required. Mark as not-applicable. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should be descriptive. RATIONALE: Clear names document intent. EVALUATION CRITERIA: method names follow descriptive patterns. DECISION: Method name 'test8' is generic and does not describe scenario/expected result; per rule 2 this is non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid verbose autogenerated tests. RATIONALE: Generated tests can be hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: signs of auto-generation like numeric test names, verbose auto-generated comments, EvoSuite runner. DECISION: The class uses EvoRunner and the test method is named 'test8' which are typical signs of test generation; per decision rules this indicates heavy generation artifacts and is non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD). RATIONALE: Improves coverage and clarity. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming. DECISION: The method lacks explicit Given-When-Then structure and only covers a single basic scenario; per rule 3 (minimal tests -> non-compliant). VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should verify behavior via public APIs. RATIONALE: Avoid brittle tests tied to internals. EVALUATION CRITERIA: no reflection or internal state access. DECISION: The test only uses public methods (new Grafo(), insereAresta, grafoTransposto, numVertices) and does not access private internals or reflection. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include messages. RATIONALE: Messages make failures easier to diagnose. EVALUATION CRITERIA: >=50% of assertions include messages and specific assertion methods preferred. DECISION: The test has a single assertEquals without a descriptive message; per rule 1 (absence of messages) mark as non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.
practices_evaluation.original_code:
grafo0.grafoTransposto();
      assertEquals(100, grafo0.numVertices());
practices_evaluation.improved_code:
grafo.grafoTransposto();
      assertEquals("After transpose vertex count should be 100", 100, grafo.numVertices());

practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain why, not what. RATIONALE: Minimal useful comments are preferred. EVALUATION CRITERIA: no commented-out code and minimal helpful comments. DECISION: No commented-out code in the method and class-level Javadoc provides context; inline comments are minimal. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be deterministic. RATIONALE: Avoid randomness/time dependencies. EVALUATION CRITERIA: no Random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep(), etc. DECISION: The test uses no random or time-dependent calls and relies on deterministic API calls. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not leave persistent side effects. RATIONALE: Prevent inter-test dependencies. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of cleanup or only local variables. DECISION: The test only creates local Grafo and performs operations in-memory with no persistent resources or static modifications visible; no cleanup needed. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories to organize tests. RATIONALE: Enables selective execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of @Tag/@Category. DECISION: Although interfaces UnitTest and GraphTests exist, the method lacks @Category or @Tag annotations; no categorization is applied. Per decision rules mark as non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.
